title: PA National Guard provides Hurricane Harvey Relief
description: Soldiers from the Pennsylvania Army National Guard provide much needed aviation and ground transportation to Austin, Texas, Sep. 7, 2017 as the long road to recovery from Hurricane Harvey continues.
keywords: Harvey, Pennsylvania Army National Guard, Fort Indiantown Gap, Annville, PA National Guard, Pa Army National Guard, Horsham, PNG, Hurricane Harvey, Hurricane Harvey 2017, Hurricane Harvey Relief, 628th Aviation

transcript.text: - [George] While many families back home plan for
the first week of the school year, Pennsylvania guardsmen
of the 628th Aviation Support Battalion,
and the 213th Aerial Support Group plan for their first week
of Hurricane Harvey relief missions.
- This storm, obviously, is kind of
a once-in-a-lifetime thing.
We've never had an event like this on this kind of scale.
It's completely different than Sandy, it's completely
different than Katrina, just the massive amount of water
that fall and flooded that area, a major, major city
like Houston.
I don't think we've ever had anything of that scale.
- [George] Calling Austin-Bergstrom International Airport
their home away from home, aviation maintenance, medical,
logistics, and transportation elements all combined
joint forces to provide Texas with much-needed support.
- I come from the Reading area of Pennsylvania,
and heard about this mission coming down the pipe
and decided to sign up for it and help out aircraft
maintenance to support whatever they've got
going on down here.
- You're talking last Tuesday we started getting the word,
by Wednesday we were calling in, putting the plans
and the capacities together for what we thought
Texas need when they put in their request.
We packed it, and by Saturday, we're moving troops out to
the area, and by Monday we'll have our entire assets there.
- [George] After Hurricane Harvey devastated the region,
helicopters became the main battle tool with the
flexibility to move people and supplies.
- My guys, put simply, are heavy on Chinook and Black Hawk
maintenance, as well as some back shops as well,
and a lot of supply folks to help logistics portions.
- [George] Rotary-wing assets also give command leadership
the ability to push search and rescue or sustainment
missions deep into the reaches of the Houston area
unreachable by ground.
And all this flying creates a severe need for maintenance,
and Pennsylvania is positioned to deliver.
- The aircraft flying out here have been pretty much
non-stop for the last week or so with the relief efforts.
Our guys here, their job is to turn man hours into
flight hours, to get these aircraft, when they get broken,
to put them back, and put them back out in the air,
and continue the efforts.
- [George] For now, as two more hurricanes with
unpredictable paths head toward the United States,
the National Guard remains ready to respond.
And Pennsylvania guardsman are here to let all know
a normal way of life is in sight,
and the rebuilding can begin.
- These are really good women and men, and this is what
they do, they are volunteer to serve in the National Guard
and that's what they do, they help.
And this is situation where they're helping
their fellow Americans.
- [George] In Austin, Texas with the 628th Aviation Support
Battalion, I'm Master Sergeant George Roach.
